newsitem.title: DENMARK: Danish economic growth resumed - economy minister.
newsitem.headline: Danish economic growth resumed - economy minister.

text.p: The slowdown in Denmark's economic growth is over and a new upturn is under way, Danish economy minister Marianne Jelved said on Monday.
"The latest data confirms that the period of flat economic growth is now over," Jelved said in a statement accompanying her ministry's latest economic survey.

"Production, employment and investment are all showing solid growth, international surveys indicate that Denmark experienced the second biggest rise in the European Union in industrial production in the second quarter of 1996," she said.
She said Denmark now satisfied the convergence criteria for European economic and monetary union (EMU) despite the fact that it had already opted out of the project.
Jelved warned though that there were dangerous trends in Denmark's economic upturn and promised moves to curb particular public building and construction projects.
"This is a signal that we must take seriously. To avoid any overheating of the economy, the government is taking steps to dampen public sector building programmes," she said.
She reiterated the government's target of balancing the public sector budget in 1997 was still possible.

"A balanced 1997 public sector budget is within our grasp, and this will be one of the government's main targets to be realised in the upcoming negotiations with opposition parties on the 1997 state budget," Jelved stressed.
Denmark's 1997 state budget is to be passed by Christmas, following negotiations between the Social Democrat-led centre-left minority government and opposition parties due to start this month.
